q-131742.name: Question 1
q-131742.problem:
Consider the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by arc length $s.$ Find the curvature at the point where $s={\pi }^{2}$ if the unit tangent vector of the curve is given by

$$
T(s)=\frac{1}{2}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{s},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{s},\,\sqrt{3}⟩.
$$
q-131742.worked_solution:
Since we are given that the curve $r(s)$ and its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ are parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature: 

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖
$$

Now, we differentiate $T(s)$ with respect to $s$ and evaluate it at $s={\pi }^{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(s) & =\frac{1}{2}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{s}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{s}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\sqrt{3})⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{s}}{2\sqrt{s}},\,\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{s}}{2\sqrt{s}},\,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4\sqrt{s}}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{s},\,\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{s},\,0⟩ \\ {T}^{′}({\pi }^{2}) & =\frac{1}{4\sqrt{{\pi }^{2}}}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{{\pi }^{2}},\,\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{{\pi }^{2}},\,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4\pi }⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4\pi }⟨0,\,-1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we obtain the curvature:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ({\pi }^{2}) & =‖{T}^{′}({\pi }^{2})‖ \\  & =\frac{1}{4\pi }\cdot \sqrt{{0}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{4\pi }\end{aligned}
$$

Since we are given that the curve r(s) and its unit tangent vector T(s) are parametrized by the arc length s, we will use the following formula for the curvature: κ(s)=‖T′(s)‖

Now, we differentiate T(s) with respect to s and evaluate it at s=π2: T′(s)=12⟨dds(cos⁡s),dds(sin⁡s),dds(3)⟩=12⟨−sin⁡s2s,cos⁡s2s,0⟩=14s⟨−sin⁡s,cos⁡s,0⟩T′(π2)=14π2⟨−sin⁡π2,cos⁡π2,0⟩=14π⟨−sin⁡π,cos⁡π,0⟩=14π⟨0,−1,0⟩

q-131732.name: Question 2
q-131732.problem:
Consider the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by arc length $s.$ Find the curvature at the point where $s=0$ if the unit tangent vector of the curve is given by

$$
T(s)=\frac{1}{5}⟨-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{10}),\,4\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{10}),\,3⟩.
$$
q-131732.worked_solution:
Since we are given that the curve $r(s)$ and its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ are parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature: 

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖
$$

Now, we differentiate $T(s)$ with respect to $s$ and evaluate it at $s=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(s) & =\frac{1}{5}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{10})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(4\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{10})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(3)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨-\frac{2}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{10}),\,-\frac{2}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{10}),\,0⟩ \\  & =-\frac{2}{25}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{10}),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{10}),\,0⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(0) & =-\frac{2}{25}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(0),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(0),\,0⟩ \\  & =-\frac{2}{25}⟨1,0,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we obtain the curvature:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(0) & =‖{T}^{′}(0)‖ \\  & =\frac{2}{25}\cdot \sqrt{{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{25}\end{aligned}
$$

q-80521.name: Question 3
q-80521.problem:
Consider the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by arc length $s.$ Find the curvature at the point where $s=2{\pi }^{2}$ if the unit tangent vector of the curve is given by

 

$$
T(s)=\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{2s}\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{2s}\,j.
$$
q-80521.worked_solution:
Since we are given that the curve $r(s)$ and its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ are parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖
$$

Now, we differentiate $T(s)$ with respect to $s$ and evaluate it at $s=2{\pi }^{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{2s})\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{2s})\,j \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{2s}}{\sqrt{2s}}\,i+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{2s}}{\sqrt{2s}}\,j \\ {T}^{′}(2{\pi }^{2}) & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{2(2{\pi }^{2})}}{\sqrt{2(2{\pi }^{2})}}\,i+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{2(2{\pi }^{2})}}{\sqrt{2(2{\pi }^{2})}}\,j \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )}{2\pi }\,i+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi )}{2\pi }\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{2\pi }\,j\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we obtain the curvature:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(2{\pi }^{2}) & =‖{T}^{′}(2{\pi }^{2})‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{(0)}^{2}+{(\frac{1}{2\pi })}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\pi }\end{aligned}
$$

q-64584.name: Question 4
q-64584.problem:
Consider the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by arc length $s.$ Find the curvature at the point where $s=\frac{3\pi }{2}$ if the unit tangent vector of the curve is given by

$$
T(s)=⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{s}{3},\,\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{s}{3},\,0⟩.
$$
q-64584.worked_solution:
Since we are given that the curve $r(s)$ and its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ are both parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖
$$

Now, we differentiate $T(s)$ with respect to $s$ and evaluate it at $s=\frac{3\pi }{2}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{s}{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{s}{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{s}{3},\,-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{s}{3},\,0⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(\frac{3\pi }{2}) & =⟨-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{3\pi }{2}),\,-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{3\pi }{2}),\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-\frac{1}{3},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain the curvature:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(\frac{3\pi }{2}) & =‖{T}^{′}(\frac{3\pi }{2})‖=\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{(-\frac{1}{3})}^{2}+{0}^{2}}=\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

q-131743.problem:
Consider the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by arc length $s.$ Find the curvature at the point where $s=\frac{\pi }{4}$ if the unit tangent vector of the curve is given by

$$
T(s)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡s,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡s,\,\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡s⟩.
$$
q-131743.worked_solution:
Since we are given that the curve $r(s)$ and its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ are parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature: 

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖
$$

Now, we differentiate $T(s)$ with respect to $s$ and evaluate it at $s=\frac{\pi }{4}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(s) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡s)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡s,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡s,\,-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡s⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}),\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}),\,-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},-1⟩ \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}⟨1,1,\sqrt{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we obtain the curvature:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})‖ \\  & =‖-\frac{1}{2}⟨1,1,\sqrt{2}⟩‖ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(\sqrt{2})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2 \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

q-132559.name: Question 6
q-132559.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s$, where

$$
r(s)=⟨s-2\operatorname{arctan}⁡s,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡({s}^{2}+1)⟩,\,s\ge 0.
$$
q-132559.worked_solution:
Let $T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖=‖{r}^{″}(s)‖
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(s)$ and ${r}^{″}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(s-2\operatorname{arctan}⁡s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({s}^{2}+1))⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{{s}^{2}-1}{{s}^{2}+1},\,\frac{2s}{{s}^{2}+1}⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{{s}^{2}-1}{{s}^{2}+1}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{2s}{{s}^{2}+1})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{4s}{({s}^{2}+1)^{2}},\,\frac{2(1-{s}^{2})}{({s}^{2}+1)^{2}}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{({s}^{2}+1)^{2}}⟨4s,\,2(1-{s}^{2})⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(s) & =‖{r}^{″}(s)‖ \\  & =\frac{1}{({s}^{2}+1)^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{(4s)^{2}+{(2(1-{s}^{2}))}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{({s}^{2}+1)^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{16{s}^{2}+4{s}^{4}-8{s}^{2}+4} \\  & =\frac{1}{({s}^{2}+1)^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{4{s}^{4}+8{s}^{2}+4} \\  & =\frac{1}{({s}^{2}+1)^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{4({s}^{2}+1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2({s}^{2}+1)}{({s}^{2}+1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{{s}^{2}+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-131945.name: Question 7
q-131945.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s$, where

$$
r(s)=⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\frac{4}{5}s⟩,\,0\le s<10\pi .
$$
q-131945.worked_solution:
Let $T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖=‖{r}^{″}(s)‖
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(s)$ and ${r}^{″}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{4}{5}s)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,\frac{4}{5}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,4⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =\frac{1}{5}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(4)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,0⟩ \\  & =-\frac{3}{25}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5}),\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(s) & =‖{r}^{″}(s)‖ \\  & =|-\frac{3}{25}|\cdot \sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{5})+{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{5})+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{3}{25}\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{3}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-34355.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s$, where

$$
r(s)=⟨\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}},\,3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}}),\,3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}})⟩,\,0\le s<2\sqrt{10}\,\pi .
$$
q-34355.worked_solution:
Let $T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖=‖{r}^{″}(s)‖
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(s)$ and ${r}^{″}(s)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}}))⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}},\,-3\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}}),\,3\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}})⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}⟨1,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}}),\,3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}})⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(1),\,-3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{sin}⁡\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}}),\,3\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}})⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}⟨0,\,-3\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}}),\,-3\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}})⟩ \\  & =\frac{3}{10}⟨0,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}}),\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}})⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(s) & =‖{r}^{″}(s)‖ \\  & =\frac{3}{10}\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}}))}^{2}+{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}}))}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{3}{10}\sqrt{0+{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}})+{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{\sqrt{10}})} \\  & =\frac{3}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-83657.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s$, where

$$
r(s)=⟨1+4\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{4}),\,3-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{4})⟩,\,0\le s<8\pi .
$$
q-83657.worked_solution:
Let $T(s)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the arc length $s.$ Since we are given the curve $r(s)$ parametrized by the arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(s)=‖{T}^{′}(s)‖=‖{r}^{″}(s)‖
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(s)$ and ${r}^{″}(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(1+4\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{4})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(3-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{4}))⟩ \\  & =⟨-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{4})\cdot \frac{1}{4},\,-4\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{4})\cdot \frac{1}{4}⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{4}),\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{4})⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{4})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{4}))⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{4})\cdot \frac{1}{4},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{4})\cdot \frac{1}{4}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4}⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{4}),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{4})⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(s) & =‖{r}^{″}(s)‖ \\  & =|\frac{1}{4}|\sqrt{{(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{4}))}^{2}+{(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{4}))}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{4})+{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{4})} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-131228.name: Question 11
q-131228.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(t)$ given that its derivative ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the corresponding unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$ are as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)=⟨\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{{e}^{t}},\,-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{{e}^{t}}⟩,\,{T}^{′}(t)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$
q-131228.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the derivative of the curve ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Now, we find the magnitudes of ${r}^{′}(t)$ and ${T}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \sqrt{{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡t+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \sqrt{2({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \sqrt{2} \\  & =1 \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{{e}^{t}})}^{2}+{(-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{{e}^{t}})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡t-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t}{{e}^{2t}}+\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡t+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t}{{e}^{2t}}} \\  & =\frac{1}{{e}^{t}}\cdot \sqrt{2({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{{e}^{t}}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{{e}^{t}})} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{t}}{\sqrt{2}}.\end{aligned}

q-83663.name: Question 12
q-83663.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(t)$ given that its derivative ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the corresponding unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$ are as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)=\,-12{t}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{3})i+12{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡({t}^{3})\,j,\,{T}^{′}(t)=-3{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡({t}^{3})\,i-3{t}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{3})\,j\end{aligned}
$$
q-83663.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the derivative of the curve ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Now, we find the magnitudes of ${r}^{′}(t)$ and ${T}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-12{t}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{3}))}^{2}+{(12{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡({t}^{3}))}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-12{t}^{2})^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡({t}^{3})+(12{t}^{2})^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡({t}^{3})} \\  & =\sqrt{(12{t}^{2})^{2}({sin}^{2}⁡({t}^{3})+{cos}^{2}⁡({t}^{3}))} \\  & =12{t}^{2} \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-3{t}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡({t}^{3}))}^{2}+{(-3{t}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡({t}^{3}))}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-3{t}^{2})^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡({t}^{3})+(-3{t}^{2})^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡({t}^{3})} \\  & =\sqrt{(3{t}^{2})^{2}({sin}^{2}⁡({t}^{3})+{cos}^{2}⁡({t}^{3}))} \\  & =3{t}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{3{t}^{2}}{12{t}^{2}}=\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-131230.name: Question 13
q-131230.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point $t>0$ on the curve $r(t)$ given that its derivative ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the corresponding unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$ are as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)=⟨2t,\,-3{t}^{2}⟩,\,{T}^{′}(t)=-\frac{6}{(9{t}^{2}+4)^{3/2}}⟨3t,\,2⟩,\,t\ge 0\end{aligned}
$$
q-131230.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the derivative of the curve ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Now, we find the magnitudes of ${r}^{′}(t)$ and ${T}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{6}{(9{t}^{2}+4)^{3/2}}\cdot \sqrt{{(3t)}^{2}+{(2)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{6}{(9{t}^{2}+4)^{3/2}}\cdot \sqrt{9{t}^{2}+4} \\  & =\frac{6}{9{t}^{2}+4} \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(2t)}^{2}+{(-3{t}^{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+9{t}^{4}} \\  & =t\sqrt{9{t}^{2}+4}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{6}{9{t}^{2}+4})}{t\sqrt{9{t}^{2}+4}} \\  & =\frac{6}{t(9{t}^{2}+4)^{3/2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-64661.problem:
Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(t)$ given that its derivative ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the corresponding unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$ are as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t)=-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,i+2\,j-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,k,\,{T}^{′}(t)=-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,i+\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,k\end{aligned}
$$
q-64661.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the derivative of the curve ${r}^{′}(t)$ and the derivative of the unit tangent ${T}^{′}(t)$, we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Now, we find the magnitudes of ${r}^{′}(t)$ and ${T}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}+{(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2({cos}^{2}⁡2t+{sin}^{2}⁡2t)} \\  & =\sqrt{2} \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4({sin}^{2}⁡2t+{cos}^{2}⁡2t)+4} \\  & =\sqrt{4\cdot 2} \\  & =2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the curvature is 

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2\sqrt{2}}=\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-34177.name: Question 15
q-34177.problem: Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve $r(t)=⟨t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t,t\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩$ for $t>0.$
q-34177.worked_solution:
Let $T(t)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the parameter t. Since we are given the curve r(t) parametrized by the parameter 
t (not the arc length s), we will use the following formula for the curvature

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and find its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\  & =⟨t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ &  \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =t\end{aligned}
$$

since $t>0.$ 

Hence, the corresponding unit tangent vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and find its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, the curvature for  $t>0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{1}{t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the curvature at an arbitrary point on the curve r(t)=⟨tsin⁡t+cos⁡t,tcos⁡t−sin⁡t⟩ for t>0.

a

b

Correct
EXPLANATION

Let T(t) denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the parameter t. Since we are given the curve r(t) parametrized by the parameter t (not the arc length s), we will use the following formula for the curvature κ(t)=‖T′(t)‖‖r′(t)‖

Now, we calculate r′(t) and find its magnitude:

r′(t)=⟨ddt(tsin⁡t+cos⁡t),ddt(tcos⁡t−sin⁡t)⟩=⟨sin⁡t+tcos⁡t−sin⁡t,cos⁡t−tsin⁡t−cos⁡t⟩=⟨tcos⁡t,−tsin⁡t⟩‖r′(t)‖=(tcos⁡t)2+(−tsin⁡t)2=t2(cos2⁡t+sin2⁡t)=t

since t>0.

Hence, the corresponding unit tangent vector is

T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖=⟨cos⁡t,−sin⁡t⟩.

Next, we calculate T′(t) and find its magnitude: T′(t)=⟨ddt(cos⁡t),ddt(−sin⁡t)⟩=⟨−sin⁡t,−cos⁡t⟩‖T′(t)‖=(−sin⁡t)2+(−cos⁡t)2=1

Finally, the curvature for t>0 is

κ(t)=‖T′(t)‖‖r′(t)‖=1t.
